data.narrative:
Anthrogen is a seed-stage biotech company founded by Ankit Singhal, Connor Lee, and Vignesh Karthik, having raised $4M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public biotech peers (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private-stage biotech companies, including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Of three triangulation methods examined, only stage-progression analysis proved applicable. The peer-median approach was inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the biotech sector—while 7 same-sector peers exist, none met the minimum threshold of 3 datapoints in narrow valuation tiers. Public-comp anchoring was also inapplicable because Anthrogen's revenue remains undisclosed, precluding use of the sector's 6.2x median P/S multiple across the three public comps. The stage-progression method applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier to the $4M total raised as a proxy base value, implying a $10M post-money valuation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $8M to $12M, with a median point estimate of $10M. This range reflects high uncertainty inherent in deriving value from a single applicable method. The primary limitations are the absence of close-stage private comparables with disclosed valuations and Anthrogen's lack of revenue disclosure, both typical constraints in early-stage biotech. Validation would require either additional peer transaction data or disclosure of revenue or clinical milestone progress.
